title: One step, two jobs
author: Claude (ChessProblemHelper)
source: Original, composed 11 October 2026 (on request of E. Bourd)
teaser: Ten units and a quiet pawn key. The pawn has two things to do, and only one square lets it do both.

comment.what: The key is a pawn single step with two jobs. On c3 the pawn protects d4, so the threat 2.Qd4# works. Leaving c2, it opens the bishop's diagonal b1-f5, which two mates use: 1...Se4 2.Qxe4# and 1...Sxf5 2.Rxf5# (in the set play 1...Sxf5 has no mate). The knight g7 defends twice by guarding d4, and each time the half-battery Rh5/Pf5 answers.
flaws: Random moves of the knight f2 (Sg4, Sh3, Sh1, Sd1) unguard e4, so 2.Qe4# mates as well as the threat. Duals after unthematic moves.
No tries. The planned 1.c4? (the double step) never existed: the queen stands on c4.
The white king h8 takes no part; it only stands off the knights' checks.
Mixed defences: two guard d4, one blocks e4. No common motive (the critique's 'second-layer unity missing').
pluses: A quiet key with two reasons.
Three different mates, one of them (Rxf5) added by the key.
7+3, and the trim tool cannot remove any unit.
comment.process: Idea on paper, two kernels, one defender search, one cleaning step: about 25 minutes, 9 solves, 1 search. The stages with their diagrams are below.
comment.lesson: Test the planned try at the kernel stage, not at judging: the queen's post chosen for the box killed the double-step try, and nobody noticed for five stages.

development.title: Why would a pawn step be the only key?
development.change: Three reasons: open a line for a piece behind it, give a flight, guard a square the threat needs. Choice: Bb1 behind Pc2, black king e5; 1.c3 opens b1-f5 and guards d4. Planned threat 2.Qe4#, planned try 1.c4? (the double step guards d5, not d4).

development.title: Box the king, no Black men
development.change: Se8 guards d6, f6; Pf5 guards e6; Pg4 protects f5; Qc4 holds d4, e4, f4, d5, e6.
development.verdict: No solution: every White move stalemates or frees a square.
development.decision: Black needs a unit whose moves defend.

development.title: Add a black knight f2
development.change: +bSf2: Sd3 would cut b1-e4, Se4 blocks, Sxg4 unguards f5.
development.decision: Move the White king out of reach.

development.title: King to h8: the kernel is sound
development.decision: The planned threat was wrong (Sf2 guards e4); the solver's is better: the pawn guards d4 for the threat, the opened line serves the mate after Se4. One defence only: add defenders.

development.title: One Black and one White unit around the kernel
development.change: kernel_search 1 1 with the key c2-c3 fixed: 39,090 positions, 74 hits, 44 seconds.

hits.caption: +bBb4 +wRc8: Bc5 Rxc5#, Bxc3 Rc5#. The rook mates on c5 twice.
+bSc7 +wRf6: Se6 Rxe6#, Sb5 Re6#. Same square twice.
Many hits with +wPd3: the pawn blocks b1-e4, so the key opens nothing.
+bSg7 +wRh5: Se6 fxe6#, Sxf5 Rxf5#, Se4 Qxe4#. Three different mates.

development.title: Sound, with one redundant pawn
development.verdict: Sound; critique: wPg4 serves only the set play (big flaw), and Sxg4 gives duals.
development.decision: Remove g4: in the diagram Rh5 already protects f5, after the key Bb1 does.

development.title: Without g4
development.verdict: Sound, 7+3, three different mates; gate PASS; trim: nothing removable.

mentor_questions: Are the duals after the random moves of Sf2 (Qe4# beside the threat) acceptable in a simple problem?
Is the key's double job (guard d4, open b1-f5 for two mates) enough content for a light #2?
